title: Build audit-and-rewrite pipeline for misattributed usage after API key rotations and subaccount joins
creator: Priya Shah
description: Several customers reported unexpected spikes and charge discrepancies following a sequence of API key rotations and a subsequent subaccount merge. Investigation shows a timing/window bug in the attribution layer: when keys rotate and subaccounts are merged within the same retention window, live meter events (token counts and embedding units) were recorded against stale key->workspace mappings and not reconciled after canonical mapping updates. This ticket builds an auditable pipeline to detect, reclassify, and rewrite misattributed usage in the accounting datastore and to add guards preventing recurrence.
steps_to_reproduce: Rotate API key A -> A' for workspace W on billing node (simulate key swap)
Create new subaccount S under org O and run traffic using rotated key A' immediately after rotation
Merge subaccount S into project P (canonical mapping change) within 1 hour of rotation
Observe billing ledger shows tokens attributed to old workspace or orphan key mapping instead of project P
Run attribution reconciliation job (current implementation) and note it does not pick up events in the window where mapping changed faster than our event-index refresh TTL
root_cause: Attribution service uses an in-memory key->workspace cache with a refresh TTL (5m) and applies attribution at write time. During rapid sequences of key rotation + subaccount merges, events are written with the old cache mapping and never backfilled. There is no idempotent replay or watermark-based reconciliation to correct historical rows after canonical mapping changes.
mitigation: Deploy short-term hotfix: lower attribution cache TTL to 30s and emit a mapping-change webhook that marks recent events for re-evaluation
Open emergency billing correction workflow for affected customers (manual credits) until rewrite completes
Add monitoring alert on spike of 'unattributed' token buckets in ledger
acceptance_criteria: A pipeline (audit-and-rewrite job) exists that: identifies candidate misattributed events, computes corrected workspace/project attribution, and writes corrected ledger rows with an audit trail
Automated end-to-end test that simulates rotation + merge scenario and verifies ledger rows are corrected
No new occurrences for 14 days in canary orgs after deployment (alerting in Grafana)
Post-deploy run completes for backlog of historical 30 days and generates a reconciliation report for Finance
